candidate_claim: God self-declaration is treated as root speech, not observer-assembled evidence.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the framework requires creature recognition before divine identity can be named.

candidate_claim: The ground publishes identity before creatures can name the ground correctly.
first_negative_guard: Reject if self-declaration is reduced to later human inference.

candidate_claim: In Exodus 20:2, identity precedes command.
first_negative_guard: Reject if law is treated as prior to divine naming in the covenant sequence.

candidate_claim: Covenant life begins with named divine identity rather than bare obligation.
first_negative_guard: Reject if covenant is modeled as command without identity-source.

candidate_claim: Old Testament I AM declarations cluster around identity, authority, covenant, uniqueness, deliverance, protection, judgment, and holiness.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the cluster cannot be textually supported across the cited examples.

candidate_claim: The Old Testament publishes the divine name before the New Testament publishes the Christ-interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the two phases are collapsed into one undifferentiated claim.

candidate_claim: The Johannine I AM statements function as interface declarations.
first_negative_guard: Reject if they are only decorative metaphors with no access role.

candidate_claim: Bread of life names divine sustenance as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if bread is treated as interchangeable with other I AM roles.

candidate_claim: Light of the world names revelation/intelligibility as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if light is treated as merely emotional inspiration.

candidate_claim: Door names access into divine presence as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if access is detached from mediation.

candidate_claim: Good shepherd names guidance and protection as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if guidance and protection are not structurally distinct from sustenance.

candidate_claim: Resurrection and life names death-defeat as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if resurrection is reduced to moral inspiration.

candidate_claim: Way, truth, and life unite path, reality, and vitality in one Christ-interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if way/truth/life can be separated without loss.

candidate_claim: True vine names source-union and fruitfulness as a creature-facing interface.
first_negative_guard: Reject if fruitfulness is modeled without continuing source-union.

candidate_claim: Bread, light, door, shepherd, resurrection, way/truth/life, and vine are irreducible roles rather than synonyms.
first_negative_guard: Reject if one role can replace every other role without remainder.

candidate_claim: The New Testament I AM declarations fulfill rather than replace the Old Testament identity declarations.
first_negative_guard: Reject if fulfillment erases Old Testament identity and authority.

candidate_claim: Manna maps to bread of life through received sustenance from above.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the preserved structure is not sustenance.

candidate_claim: Pillar of fire maps to light of the world through divine illumination and guidance.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the preserved structure is not illumination/guidance.

candidate_claim: Tabernacle door maps to I am the door through mediated entry into holy presence.
first_negative_guard: Reject if entry is unmediated.

candidate_claim: Psalm 23 shepherd maps to good shepherd through personal guidance and protection.
first_negative_guard: Reject if shepherding is not personal or protective.

candidate_claim: Passover lamb maps to resurrection and life through life preserved by given life.
first_negative_guard: Reject if substitution/given-life structure is absent.

candidate_claim: Red Sea passage maps to the way through a path opened where creatures could not open one.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the path is creature-generated.

candidate_claim: Tree of life / vine imagery maps to true vine through life by union with source.
first_negative_guard: Reject if life is modeled apart from source-union.

candidate_claim: The words change across testaments while the preserved structure remains stable.
first_negative_guard: Reject if vocabulary continuity is required instead of structural continuity.

candidate_claim: Old Testament narrative types can be read as constants running before direct axiom naming.
first_negative_guard: Reject if typology is treated as proof without structural preservation.

candidate_claim: DG1 distinguishes root claims by absence of deeper predicate or external source.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the root claim depends on a lower explanatory layer.

candidate_claim: I AM WHO I AM satisfies the DG1 root-layer signature.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the name is interpreted as caused by a prior layer.

candidate_claim: DG8 filters denial by asking whether denial depends on the thing denied.
first_negative_guard: Reject if denial can borrow the denied condition without consequence.

candidate_claim: Ordinary power claims such as king/general fail the DG8 root-dependency test.
first_negative_guard: Reject if political authority becomes structurally necessary to deny political authority.

candidate_claim: Denial of "I am the truth" still depends on truth conditions.
first_negative_guard: Reject if meaningful denial can avoid truth conditions entirely.

candidate_claim: Denial of "I am the life" is made by a living conscious agent.
first_negative_guard: Reject if the denial can be made without life or agency.

candidate_claim: Denial of "I am the light" depends on intelligibility.
first_negative_guard: Reject if denial can be meaningful without intelligibility.

candidate_claim: A Layer 0 signature appears when a claim names a condition its denial must borrow.
first_negative_guard: Reject if borrowing is merely rhetorical and not structurally required.

candidate_claim: Closure structure exposes dependency but does not mechanically force faith.
first_negative_guard: Reject if formal grammar is treated as coercive salvation.
